claims.harm: Disabling network activity drops existing anchors on a subsequent clean shutdown if no new connections were made.
claims.quote: This seems like a bug... Maybe we should re-save the original anchors if there's no new ones at a clean shutdown?
claims.settled_by_quote: I just changed the approach of this PR and changed PR title and description. It addresses concerns like https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/34213#discussion_r2718514479.

claims.harm: A race condition between setting fNetworkActive to false and socket disconnection allows ThreadSocketHandler to clear connections before block-relay peers are captured into m_anchors.
claims.quote: currently there is a data race, you should first save the anchors, and only then set `fNetworkActive = active`
claims.settled_by_quote: Fixed data race when disabling the network and saving the anchors.

claims.harm: ThreadOpenConnections continues popping and discarding anchors while network activity is disabled, leading to empty anchors upon shutdown.
claims.quote: ThreadOpenConnections() still consumes m_anchors while networking is disabled. It pops an address before calling OpenNetworkConnection(), which then returns because fNetworkActive is false.
claims.settled_by_quote: Looks pretty nice to me now, thanks for addressing my comments.

claims.harm: Anchors saved on network deactivation were not capped to the oldest peers, allowing a newly added block-relay peer to displace older anchors.
claims.quote: GetCurrentBlockRelayOnlyConns() returns peers in connection order, while ThreadOpenConnections() consumes anchors from the back... Including a temporary third peer therefore lets it take the oldest anchor’s place after a network toggle.

support.reason: I think this is a good improvement, makes sense to have, and I can’t find any additional surface of attack introduced here... low risk, and would avoid unnecessarily losing anchors.

Disabling networking should not cause the node to lose its anchors. Preserving them across a clean shutdown lets the node reconnect when networking resumes, increasing eclipse attack resilience on restarts.

result.notes: Initial read of PR 34213. All four objections—luke-jr's note on preserving anchors across shutdowns, danielabrozzoni's race condition fix, willcl-ark's offline anchor consumption bug, and w0xlt's anchor capping patch—were resolved with code updates. Bortlesboat was excluded from support as an automated bot account.
